relationships.subject: capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 can be activated by capsaicin, heat >43 °C, shifts in proton concentrations that includes extracellular acidosis and intracellular alkalosis

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: The consecutive action potential transmission causes neuropeptide release from nociceptors, such as calcitonin gene-related peptide or substance P, that ultimately sends pain signals to the brain as well as activates neurogenic inflammation [6].

relationships.subject: resiniferatoxin
relationships.evidence_quote: Both capsaicin and RTX are naturally occurring irritants that share a common homovanillyl group. This shared chemical structure allows both agonists to target TRPV1.

key_findings: TRPV1 agonists (capsaicin, RTX, CNTX-4975, vocacapsaicin) act by overactivation leading to desensitization or chemo-axotomy, while antagonists are limited by hyperthermia and burn risk.
The capsaicin 8% patch is FDA-approved for postherpetic neuralgia and diabetic neuropathy, giving about 30% pain reduction for about 12 weeks.
